newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Eko Stahl aims for breakeven in 1998.
newsitem.headline: German Eko Stahl aims for breakeven in 1998.

text.p: East German steel company Eko Stahl GmbH aims to at least break even in 1998, chief executive Hans-Joachim Krueger told reporters on Wednesday at the opening of a new blast furnace.

The troubled steel maker, in which Belgium's Cockerill Sambre took a 60 percent stake in January 1995, posted a 123 million mark ($73.6 million) loss in 1996 and expects to post another loss of unspecified size this year, Krueger said.

Eko's sales in 1997 are seen at 1.423 billion marks, and roughly the same again in 1998, he said. The workforce is now about 2,600 and should hold steady even after the new blast furnace begins operation, he said.

Parent company Cockerill reported last week it plunged into the red in 1996, weighed down by an extraordinary loss, but it was hopeful of a small profit in 1997. Cockerill has an option to buy the rest of Eko from Germany's BvS privatisation agency by the end of 1999.
Krueger said steel prices had bottomed out and had begun to rebound in some sectors.
The new blast furnace has a capacity of 4,100 tonnes a day, and will reduce air pollution. A new hot rolling mill is also due to start up in summer.
-- Terence Gallagher, Frankfurt Newsroom, 49 69 7565 1210 ($ = 1.670 German Marks)
